answer: Sybil resistance here is stake-weighted identity: each agent locks a non-divisible, slashable bond and needs vouchers from already-verified peers before its votes count. Influence tracks verified unique identities, not account count, so splitting one wallet into a thousand keys buys nothing extra: every forged node pays its own bond and recruits its own vouchers. An attacker riding the tide of cheap signups hits a cost ridge, since outlays climb linearly with each new identity while payoff stays flat, like trying to build a mountain by piling one knoll on another.
